one_liner: Fine-tune a base model into an instruction-follower via response-only loss masking, with data curation and forgetting mitigation.

key_terms.definition: Training a pretrained model on (instruction, response) pairs with maximum-likelihood loss to teach instruction-following, format, and helpful behavior.
Setting instruction tokens' labels to an ignore index so gradients flow only from response tokens, concentrating the SFT signal on reply quality.
Degradation of a model's prior general capabilities when fine-tuning updates overwrite weights that encoded broader pretraining knowledge.
Study showing 1,000 curated (instruction, response) pairs can outperform SFT on hundreds of thousands of noisy examples, motivating data quality over quantity.
The idea that a model's knowledge comes almost entirely from pretraining; SFT merely teaches it to access and present that knowledge in the right format.
The standard pipeline of SFT, then reward modeling, then RL-based policy optimization (PPO or DPO), each stage building on the previous one.
A safety-data recipe that mixes a small fraction of refusal/safe-completion examples with benign 'comply' contrast examples to calibrate harm refusal without causing over-refusal.
A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes base weights and learns a low-rank update ΔW = AB added to a weight matrix during training.
A LoRA variant that additionally quantizes the frozen base model to 4-bit NF4, enabling SFT of large models on a single consumer GPU.
Fine-tuning approaches, like LoRA, that freeze most pretrained weights and train only a small adapter, drastically cutting memory and forgetting risk.
An 80-question multi-turn benchmark, scored by an LLM judge on a 1-10 scale, used to evaluate instruction-tuned models' reasoning, coding, and writing quality.
Accumulating gradients over several mini-batches before an optimizer step, increasing effective batch size without increasing peak memory.

prerequisites: causal language modeling / next-token prediction objective
